bounds: Two grants, three credential identities, one absent-credential sentinel, two sweeps, two batches per sweep, batch sizes 1 and 2, and clock 0..3. Fifteen initial classes include shared/foreign/missing references, malformed lifecycle data, and valid/invalid tombstones.
fairness: Weak fairness settles started sweeps. Repeated cron scheduling and eventual removal of corrupt rows are not promised.
limitations: Two grants, three credential identities, one absent-credential sentinel, two sweeps, two batches per sweep, batch sizes 1 and 2, and clock 0..3. Fifteen initial classes include shared/foreign/missing references, malformed lifecycle data, and valid/invalid tombstones.

Grant ordering is the source lexicographic expiry/creation/id order represented by distinct expiry/id ranks. Creation ranks are fixed. Deleted future timestamps outside the clock horizon are represented by an invalid-time flag.
One pre-admitted acknowledgement or owner rewrite per grant may race the planner. Row locks exclude competing commits. Key and reference checks follow row locking.
Live reference counts include both modeled grants. Arbitrary new references introduced by privileged SQL, unbounded backlogs and concurrent cleanup workers are outside this instance.
Grant lifecycle validity and credential provenance group their exact source field comparisons into predicates. Secret bytes, cryptography and inference-policy admission remain external.
Weak fairness settles started sweeps. Repeated cron scheduling and eventual removal of corrupt rows are not promised.

assumptions: Checked formula in MobileAppGrantCleanup_one: SweepsSettle = and { Plan.weakFair(s), LockRows.weakFair(s), LockKeys.weakFair(s), Classify.weakFair(s), Commit.weakFair(s) } implies eventually(always(Set("idle", "done").contains(s.phase)))
The property is conditional on its written model fairness and environmental premises. Real scheduler fairness, provider completion and implementation refinement are not proved.
